items.title: An extension of K(A,k) by K(A,k+1) built from the index sets
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file simplicial.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-extension at source lines 3772-3794: for an object A of an abelian category and k at least 0, the simplicial object E whose n-simplices are the direct sum of copies of A indexed by the maps [n] to [k+1] with image [k] or [k+1] fits into a short exact sequence 0 to K(A,k) to E to K(A,k+1) to 0 which is term by term split. The proof at source lines 3796-3802 is a three-sentence construction check: the two maps are the inclusion and projection of the obvious direct summands, their composure properties are read off from the inclusions of index sets, and they are visibly morphisms of simplicial objects because the structure maps are induced by composition of indices. The card's substance is therefore the construction itself, which the statement spells out in full.
